title: Mesa 26.1.7 doubles Vulkan throughput on Intel Arc B580 (Battlemage) — 30 → 67 tok/s
body:
# Mesa 26.1.7 doubles llama.cpp Vulkan throughput on Intel Arc B580 (Battlemage)

Swapping only the Intel Vulkan driver — Mesa **26.0.8 → 26.1.7** — took Ollama from ~30 to ~67 tok/s on an Arc B580. Same GPU, same kernel, same model, same context,
 same quantization. Nothing else on the machine changed.

The kernel turned out to be irrelevant, which was the opposite of what I expected going in.

Charts and full methodology: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/858caefa-9680-4bda-a038-f527065df867

## Results

400-token decode, three seeds per driver, throughput from Ollama's `eval_count / eval_duration`.

| Model | Architecture | ctx | Mesa 26.0.8 | Mesa 26.1.7 | Gain |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `gemma4:latest` (E4B, Q4_K_M) | per-layer embeddings, 5:1 SWA | 131072 | 30.25 | **66.99** | 2.21× |
| `qwen3:8b` | dense, standard GQA | 8192 | 29.79 | **61.01** | 2.05× |

```
decode throughput, tok/s (higher is better)

gemma4  Mesa 26.0.8  ███████████████████·························  30.25
gemma4  Mesa 26.1.7  ██████████████████████████████████████████··  66.99
qwen3   Mesa 26.0.8  ███████████████████·························  29.79
qwen3   Mesa 26.1.7  ██████████████████████████████████████······  61.01
```

Individual runs:

```
gemma4  26.0.8 : 30.55, 30.25, 29.95
gemma4  26.1.7 : 67.09, 67.30, 66.59
qwen3   26.0.8 : 29.61, 29.89, 29.87
qwen3   26.1.7 : 60.35, 61.33, 61.36
```

The two models share almost nothing structurally — gemma4 E4B keeps ~5.9 GB of per-layer embedding weights in host RAM by design and caps 35 of its 42 layers at a 51
2-token sliding window; qwen3:8b is a conventional dense model fully resident on the GPU. Both roughly double, so this isn't an artifact of one architecture.

## Context scaling: a cliff on the old driver that disappears

On 26.0.8, gemma4 held ~34 tok/s up to 32k context and then stepped down to ~30 and stayed there. On 26.1.7 the curve is flat to the model's full window.

| num_ctx | 26.0.8 | 26.1.7 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 4,096 | 34.41 | 67.39 |
| 32,768 | 34.45 | 66.47 |
| 49,152 | 29.61 | 66.99 |
| 131,072 | 30.18 | 67.08 |

Caveat: qwen3 was flat on *both* drivers across 4k–32k (29.87→29.89 and 61.27→61.34), but its KV cache grows linearly with no sliding-window cap, so contexts past 32
k exceed 12 GB. **The cliff was only observed on one model** and may not generalize.

## The kernel made no difference

This began as a kernel experiment — I'd read that Battlemage improvements needed 7.2. Mainline 7.2.0 vs Ubuntu 7.0.0-30, Mesa 26.1.7 on both, gemma4 at 128k:

| Kernel | tok/s |
|---|---:|
| 7.0.0-30-generic (Ubuntu) | 66.86 |
| 7.2.0-070200 (mainline) | 67.00 |

+0.21%, well inside noise. The gain is entirely userspace; `xe` on 7.0 submits to Battlemage just as well. Pairing 26.1 with a newer kernel was not necessary.

## Setup

- Intel Arc B580 (BMG G21), 12 GB, `xe` driver
- Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0-30-generic
- Ollama 0.33.0 (ships `libggml-vulkan.so`; Vulkan enabled by default on discrete GPUs)
- Mesa 26.0.8-1ubuntu0.3 (Ubuntu archive) vs 26.1.7~kisak1~r (kisak-mesa PPA)
- B580 drives no displays (AMD 760M iGPU runs the desktop), so 10,955 MiB free for compute in every run

## Method

Both drivers were tested through a second Ollama instance on port 11435, identical except `VK_DRIVER_FILES` pointing at a different ICD. System Mesa was never modifi
ed.

- Full GPU offload confirmed from the loader log each run (43/43 gemma4, 37/37 qwen3)
- Free VRAM verified identical (10,955 MiB) before each measurement
- Instances stopped with SIGTERM and drained to zero `llama-server` processes between cases

**Trap worth repeating:** SIGKILL on `ollama serve` orphans its `llama-server` child, which keeps holding VRAM. The next instance then sees less free memory and *sil
ently* partial-offloads — one early run gave 22/43 layers and 13.5 tok/s with no error anywhere. Always check the offload line rather than trusting the number.

## What this doesn't establish

I could not identify the mechanism. Four extensions are new in 26.1.7 on this device:

```
VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2
VK_EXT_present_timing
VK_EXT_device_address_binding_report
VK_KHR_internally_synchronized_queues
```

`VK_NV_cooperative_matrix2` was the obvious suspect, since ggml-vulkan has a dedicated coopmat2 matmul path. **It isn't the cause** — running 26.1.7 with `GGML_VK_DI
SABLE_COOPMAT2=1` gave 67.5 tok/s, unchanged. Vulkan API level also moved 1.4.335 → 1.4.354.

Other limits:

- One machine, one GPU. Untested on A-series, other Battlemage SKUs, or iGPUs.
- Two models, both quantized. No fp16 or MoE runs.
- Prefill was not the focus; it sat near 136 tok/s on both drivers and barely moved.
- Mesa 26.1.x was not bisected, so the change could have landed anywhere in that series.

If anyone knows what changed in ANV between 26.0 and 26.1 that would produce this, I'd like to hear it.

## Testing it without touching system Mesa

A newer ANV can be dropped into a private prefix and handed to one process via `VK_DRIVER_FILES`, leaving the desktop driver alone:

```bash
# extract the driver only, no install
dpkg-deb -x mesa-vulkan-drivers_26.1.7~kisak1~r_amd64.deb prefix/

# ICD pointing at the extracted .so by absolute path
cat > icd.json <<'EOF'
{"ICD":{"api_version":"1.4.354",
 "library_path":"/opt/mesa-26.1.7/lib/libvulkan_intel.so"},
 "file_format_version":"1.0.1"}
EOF

# confirm which driver actually loads
VK_DRIVER_FILES=$PWD/icd.json vulkaninfo --summary | grep driverInfo

# point only ollama at it, via a systemd drop-in
systemctl edit ollama
# Environment="VK_DRIVER_FILES=/opt/mesa-26.1.7/share/vulkan/icd.d/intel_icd.json"
```

Check `driverInfo` before trusting any result. An empty or mistyped path falls back to the system driver silently, and then you're benchmarking nothing. That happene
d to me once — an install script copied the system driver into a directory named for the new one, and only the `vulkaninfo` check caught it.
